observed.description: SubagentLifecycle reserves active work by canonical task_id alone. Two independent parents using the same child-local task_id therefore conflict even though parent_turn_id and target make them distinct delegated identities.
example: parent-B -> notion child-1 is rejected before provider work with delegated task_id is already active
observed.batch_variant: run_many also rejects duplicate canonical task_id values without considering parent_turn_id or target.
observed.existing_tests_gap: Current duplicate-id tests use the same parent. There is no regression proving equal child-local task ids under distinct parents/targets can coexist.

integration_risk: Independent parent turns can spuriously block each other's delegated work.
A future Qwen adapter under the same neutral lifecycle inherits the same false conflict across providers.
Using bare task_id for lifecycle reservation disagrees with the required parent-scoped persistent identity needed for restart-safe Qwen taskId/batchId/sessionPrefix derivation.

recommended_contract.conversation_identity: must use the same parent-scoped canonical identity; provider account/thread ids remain excluded
